spacr.gene_measurement_compare.aggregate:
One row per gene: the median of its guides' medians.

:param guides: the table :func:`aggregate_guides` returns.
:param features: the feature columns to reduce.
:returns: ``gene, n_guides, n_cells, [mitotic_cells, mitotic_index,]
    <features>``. The mitotic index pools the gene's cells -- mitotic
    cells over all cells -- which is how the published per-gene
    ``mitotic_index`` is defined.

One row per guide: its gene, cell count and per-feature medians.

:param cells: one row per cell, already normalised if wanted.
:param features: the columns to summarise.
:param guide: the guide column.
:param gene: the gene column.
:param mitotic: an optional boolean column; its mean becomes
    ``mitotic_fraction`` and its sum ``mitotic_cells``.
:returns: ``guide, gene, n_cells, [mitotic_cells, mitotic_fraction,]
    <features>``.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.bootstrap:
Two-sided P values per gene against non-targeting controls.

:param control_values: one row per non-targeting cell, ``features``
    columns, on the same scale as the guide medians.
:param guides: :func:`aggregate_guides` output for the genes to test.
:param features: the features to test.
:param n_boot: simulated or bootstrap replicates; P values resolve to
    ``1 / (n_boot + 1)``.
:param seed: the random seed, so a rerun gives the same table.
:param max_cells: the cell bootstrap caps a guide's draw at this many
    cells. The median of a larger draw barely moves, and the cost is
    linear in it. The calibrated null does not use it.
:param null: ``'calibrated'`` or ``'cell_bootstrap'``.
:param control_guides: :func:`aggregate_guides` output for the
    non-targeting guides. The calibrated null needs it.
:returns: ``gene`` plus ``<feature>_pvalue`` and ``<feature>_fdr``
    (Benjamini-Hochberg across genes) per feature. With the calibrated
    null, ``attrs["null"]`` holds each feature's centre, cell variance
    and between-guide variance.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown ``null``, or for the calibrated null
    without ``control_guides``.

BOTH NULLS REPEAT THE GENE'S OWN SAMPLING. The gene statistic is the
median of its guide medians. Each null draws one value per guide of the
gene, sized like that guide, and takes their median.

THE CALIBRATED NULL IS THE DEFAULT. Each simulated guide median is drawn
from a normal distribution centred on the median of the non-targeting
guides. Its variance is ``between + pi / 2 * cell / n``. Here ``n`` is
the guide's cell count and ``cell`` is the squared robust standard
deviation of the control cells. The ``between`` term is the variance
the non-targeting guide medians show beyond cell sampling. Cells of one
guide share wells, fields and clonal patches, so in an optical pooled
screen that term is large.

THE CELL BOOTSTRAP IGNORES THE BETWEEN-GUIDE VARIANCE. It draws as many
non-targeting cells as each guide has and takes their median, which is
the construction of Funk et al. 2022. Its null therefore holds only
cell-sampling noise, and its P values are too small. On one plate of the
Funk et al. 2022 screen it called 4,053 of 5,049 genes and a third of
the non-targeting guides hits. It is kept only to rerun analyses made
before spaCR 1.5.1.8.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.mitotic_c:
Mitotic cells, called from nuclear DNA intensity and nuclear area.

:param cells: one row per cell.
:param dna: the nuclear mean DNA (DAPI) intensity column.
:param area: the nuclear area column.
:param group: normalise within this column's groups.
:param dna_z: the robust z above which the DNA mean must sit.
:param area_z: the robust z the nuclear area must not exceed.
:returns: a boolean Series over ``cells``.

A mitotic nucleus is condensed chromatin: its DNA is packed into a
smaller area, so its MEAN DNA intensity is far above an interphase
nucleus's while its area is at or below the median. Both are robust z
scores against every cell of the group, so the rule needs no absolute
intensity and travels between plates. It is a deliberately simple rule:
Funk et al. 2022 trained a classifier on DNA and tubulin features, which
this does not reproduce, and a cell in early prophase or in telophase
is missed.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.robust_z_:
Each feature as a robust z against the control cells of its own group.

:param cells: one row per cell.
:param features: the numeric columns to normalise.
:param control: a boolean Series over ``cells``; True marks a control
    (non-targeting) cell.
:param group: the column whose groups are normalised separately, the
    well in an optical pooled screen.
:returns: a frame of the same index and ``features`` columns:
    ``(x - median_control) / (1.4826 * MAD_control)`` within the group.

THE CONTROLS SET THE SCALE, as in Funk et al. 2022: each well's
non-targeting cells are that well's reference, so a well-to-well shift
in staining moves the reference with it rather than reading as a
phenotype. A group whose controls have zero spread, or no controls at
all, is NaN rather than infinite.
spacr.ops_engine._ph_fields.cell_path: Where one field's cell table is kept.
spacr.ops_engine._ph_fields.mask_path: Where one field's masks are kept.
spacr.ops_merge.deduplicate_matches:
One observation per sequencing nucleus where fields overlap.

:param frame: merge rows with ``key`` and ``by`` columns.
:param key: the column that must be unique afterwards.
:param by: the column whose smallest value wins.
:returns: ``(kept, dropped)`` -- the frame with one row per ``key``,
    and how many rows were dropped.

A nucleus imaged in two overlapping phenotype fields is two
observations of one cell. Counting both would weight that cell twice in
its guide's median, so the closer match is kept; ties go to the first
row, which keeps the result independent of nothing but the input order.
spacr.ops_merge.field_to_well:
Field ``(row, column)`` points moved into the well frame.

:param points: ``(N, 2)`` points in field pixels.
:param transform: ``(scale, rotation, translation)``.
:returns: ``(N, 2)`` well-frame ``(y, x)``.
spacr.ops_merge.field_transform:
The similarity taking a phenotype field's pixels onto the well frame.

:param scale: well-frame pixels per field pixel; 0.25 on the reference
    plate, where a 2,960 px 20X field lands on 1,480 px 10X tiles.
:param degrees: the field's rotation in the well frame.
:param centre: ``(y, x)`` of the field's centre in the well frame, as
    ``ops_phenotype.centre_y/centre_x`` stores it.
:param field_shape: ``(height, width)`` of the field in its own pixels.
:returns: ``(scale, rotation, translation)``, the form
    :func:`match_cells` takes, mapping ``(row, column)`` field points to
    ``(y, x)`` well points.

The centre is what the phenotype phase predicted for the field's middle
pixel, so the translation is whatever puts ``field_shape / 2`` there
once the field is scaled and rotated.
spacr.ops_merge.merge_field:
Pair one field's nuclei with sequencing nuclei, one to one.

:param points: ``(N, 2)`` field nucleus centroids, field pixels.
:param targets: ``(M, 2)`` sequencing nucleus centroids, well pixels.
:param transform: the field's ``(scale, rotation, translation)``.
:param threshold: the largest distance still called the same nucleus,
    in well pixels.
:param gpu: passed to :func:`match_cells`.
:returns: ``(K, 3)`` float rows of ``(point_index, target_index,
    distance)``.
spacr.ops_merge.refine_field_transform:
Re-solve one field's transform on its own nuclei, or keep the seed.

:param points: ``(N, 2)`` nucleus centroids of the field, field pixels.
:param targets: ``(M, 2)`` sequencing-nucleus centroids near the field,
    well pixels.
:param seed: the stored ``(scale, rotation, translation)``.
:param radius: how close a moved nucleus must land to agree, well px.
:param min_inliers: the fewest agreeing nuclei to accept a re-solve.
:param min_fraction: the smallest share of ``points`` that must agree.
:param max_scale_change: how far the re-solved scale may move from the
    seed's, as a fraction.
:param max_degrees_change: how far its rotation may move, in degrees.
:returns: ``(transform, inliers, residual_px, refined)``; ``refined`` is
    False when the seed was kept.

THE SEED IS A RASTER PREDICTION for every field that was not an anchor,
and a few well pixels of error in it is a few nuclear radii at 10X.
Re-solving on the field's own segmented nuclei removes that error; the
bounds stop a crowded field from pulling the answer into a wrong basin,
which is the failure :func:`spacr.ops_phenotype.align_phenotype_to_sbs`
records for unconstrained scores.
spacr.ops_sample.measure_phenotype_field:
Per-cell features of one phenotype field, with spaCR's own measurement.

:param nuclei: nucleus labels, paired with ``cells`` by
    :func:`pair_nuclei_with_cells`, so nucleus ``k`` is in cell ``k``.
:param cells: cell labels.
:param image: ``(H, W, C)`` intensities.
:param channel_names: one short name per channel, used in the column
    names in place of spaCR's ``channel_<i>``.
:param texture: include the GLCM homogeneity block.
:param funk_features: add Funk et al. 2022's features: the mass
    displacement of every channel and the correlation of every channel
    pair in the nucleus and the cell (:func:`funk_object_features`),
    and ``nucleus_form_factor`` and ``cell_form_factor``,
    ``4 * pi * area / perimeter ** 2`` (``shape_features['form_factor']``
    of their ``ops/cp_emulator.py``) from spaCR's own area and
    perimeter.
:param zernike: add the Zernike moments of degree 8
    (``zernike_0`` to ``zernike_24``) of the cell and the nucleus, as
    :func:`spacr.measure._calculate_zernike` computes them with mahotas;
    the cytoplasm gets none. Needs ``spacr[zernike]``. Default False.
:returns: one row per cell, keyed by ``label``, with ``nucleus_``,
    ``cell_`` and ``cytoplasm_`` columns and the nucleus centroid as
    ``centroid_row``/``centroid_col`` in field pixels.

The features are the ones spaCR's measure writes -- morphology from
:func:`spacr.measure._morphological_measurements`, intensity and texture
from :func:`spacr.measure._intensity_measurements` -- so an OPS cell and
a measured well's cell carry the same columns and nothing is
re-derived. The cytoplasm is the cell minus its nucleus, under the
cell's label.
spacr.ops_sample.pair_nuclei_with_cells:
One nucleus per cell, both carrying the same label.

:param nuclei: a 2-D nucleus label mask.
:param cells: a 2-D cell label mask of the same field.
:returns: ``(nuclei, cells, counts)``: both relabelled ``1..K`` so that
    nucleus ``k`` lies inside cell ``k``, and how many objects were
    dropped and why.

Two independent segmentations of one field disagree at the edges: a
nucleus straddles two cells, a cell holds two nuclei, a nucleus has no
cell at all. spaCR's measurement joins a nucleus to one parent cell and
refuses a field where that is ambiguous, so the ambiguity is resolved
here: each nucleus goes to the cell it overlaps most and is clipped to
that cell; a cell keeps its largest such nucleus; cells without a
nucleus and nuclei without a cell are dropped and counted.
